description: April birthdays: zodiac signs and decans for every day of April, cusp dates, the month's numerology and its Chinese zodiac boundary.
answer: In Western astrology, April birthdays fall under Aries and Taurus. In most years April birthdays from the 1st to the 19th are Aries, and from the 20th they are Taurus. April 19, April 20 and April 21 are cusp dates. In numerology April is month 4.

sections.heading: Zodiac signs and decans in April
paragraphs: April opens in the second decan of Aries, where the Sun as sub-ruler gives the Ram warmth and a taste for recognition. Around April 10 the third decan begins, and Jupiter widens Aries' energy into a love of travel, principle and big ideas. Around April 19 or 20 the Sun crosses into Taurus. The shift is from cardinal fire to fixed earth, from sprinting to settling, and many people notice the change of pace in late-April birthdays: less urgency, more patience and a stronger interest in comfort, security and the physical world. The rest of the month sits in Taurus' first decan, where Venus rules twice over and the sign is at its most sensual and steady. April as a whole moves from the spark of an idea to the soil it needs to grow.

In most years April birthdays from the 1st to the 19th are Aries, and from the 20th they are Taurus. The cusp dates, where the sign can differ by year or time zone, are April 19, 20 and 21; each has its own page explaining both possibilities. Decan by decan, the month opens in the second decan of Aries, linked with Sun, from the 10th the third decan of Aries, linked with Jupiter and from the 20th the first decan of Taurus, linked with Venus.

sections.heading: April birthdays in numerology and the Chinese zodiac
paragraphs: April is month 4 in numerology, the number of foundations, method and dependability. It tends to add a practical, persistent note to a birth date, which suits the month's slide from Aries into Taurus. In the Chinese zodiac, April birthdays follow the animal of the calendar year, because the Lunar New Year boundary has long since passed. Four Pillars astrology adds a further layer: the Dragon month begins around April 4 or 5 with the solar term Clear and Bright, also known as Qingming, so almost every April birthday has the Dragon in its month pillar. The Dragon is traditionally associated with ambition, vitality and charisma, and it pairs naturally with both the confident Aries part of the month and the determined Taurus part that follows.
Every page for an April date lists the Life Path for several birth years, because the year changes the total even when the day stays the same.

sections.heading: Famous April birthdays
paragraphs: Each April page lists the best-known people born on that date, drawn from Wikidata and ranked by how many Wikipedia language editions have an article about them. A sample across the month: Otto von Bismarck (April 1), Maya Angelou (April 4), Jackie Chan (April 7), Steven Seagal (April 10), Thomas Jefferson (April 13), Charlie Chaplin (April 16), Ali Khamenei (April 19), Vladimir Lenin (April 22), Al Pacino (April 25) and Saddam Hussein (April 28). Sharing a birthday with someone well known says nothing about a life's direction, but it is a pleasant way into the date's sign, decan and numbers, which each page then explains in turn. The lists favour people with a precisely recorded birth date in the modern Gregorian calendar, so some much-celebrated figures from earlier centuries are missing.

faq.answer: In most years April birthdays from the 1st to the 19th are Aries, and from the 20th they are Taurus. The cusp dates, where the sign can differ by year or time zone, are April 19, 20 and 21; each has its own page explaining both possibilities.

faq.question: What is the numerology number of April?
faq.answer: April is month 4. The month is one of three parts of the Life Path calculation, with the day and the year.

faq.question: Which Chinese zodiac animal is someone born in April?
faq.answer: Lunar New Year has always passed by April, so an April birth takes the animal of the calendar birth year.
